Both widgets follow the established builtin contract (`renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult`), registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` + `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`. target.title: fix(browser): check existing-session wait navigation [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser `wait` predicates could continue in a replacement document before Browser navigation policy had approved that document. On managed Playwright, `waitForFunction` is recreated after an execution-context replacement. On existing-session Chrome MCP, the polling loop could evaluate again after navigation. A model-controlled predicate could therefore run on a policy-denied destination before the existing post-action check rejected the response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep Playwright's native in-document scheduler and async-predicate semantics, but bind each guarded wait to one document handle. Only Playwright 1.61.1's exact cross-document JSHandle error causes a retry; policy is checked before capture and again before predicate execution in the replacement document. Infrastructure and user-predicate errors are never reclassified as navigation.
- Run existing-session waits as one exact Chrome MCP session transaction. A loader-bound root UID binds the predicate to one document; session replacement fails closed before another target can be touched, and only typed tool-level stale-document errors can rebind.
- Use one aggregate timeout/abort lifecycle, dispose handles unconditionally, avoid overlapping async predicate calls, and disconnect only truly wedged guarded evaluations.
- Pin the default launcher and document-bound compatibility gate to reviewed `chrome-devtools-mcp@1.5.0`. URL-only and time-only waits remain available to custom MCP servers; document-bound waits fail with an actionable version error rather than assuming an undocumented UID contract.
- Correct the custom launcher documentation: `mcpCommand` replaces the executable/default package prefix, while `mcpArgs` append after OpenClaw-managed arguments.

## User Impact

Allowed waits retain Playwright's native polling behavior and continue across approved navigation. A wait can no longer execute its predicate in a denied replacement document or silently move to a replacement Chrome MCP session. Existing-session users get a deterministic compatibility error for unreviewed MCP versions without losing URL-only or time-only waits.

- Exact head: `97967d9847df329b42ec9fd734f60b788b913759`

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles

## What Problem This Solves

Slack message tool `delete`/`react`/`remove-reaction`/etc. actions fail with `channel_not_found` because the channel ID is lowercased during target resolution before being passed to the Slack Web API. | src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.ts | Add `shouldApplyResolvedTargetArg()` helper that compares raw input vs resolved output (after stripping kind prefixes). When the only difference is character case, preserve the raw input. Directory and plugin resolutions always apply since they carry real canonical IDs. |

target.title: feat(android): add safe cron job management
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw for Android could list cron jobs and show basic details, but it could not safely manage them. Operators had to switch to another client to inspect history, run a job, edit it, enable or disable it, or delete it.

This clean maintainer replacement supersedes #101882 after a protocol, concurrency, authorization, and accessibility rewrite. It preserves @snowzlmbot's contribution through commit co-authorship.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add typed Android models for cron details, history, mutation patches, and the closed `cron.run` result variants.
- Send minimal `cron.update` patches so untouched gateway-owned fields remain intact; explicit model and thinking clears remain explicit nulls.
- Keep detail and history generations independent so stale responses cannot overwrite a newly selected job.
- Serialize mutations and retain the busy state through the awaited list refresh, preventing the UI from presenting a second action while the runtime mutex is still locked.
- Scope delete cleanup to the job actually deleted, so deleting one job cannot clear a newer selection or history request.
- Gate mutation controls on `operator.admin` while preserving read-only detail/history access, with truthful guidance for requesting and approving admin access.
- Add persistent visible labels, accessibility semantics, disabled styling, and admin/busy gating to every editor control.
- Validate command payload arguments as JSON strings and represent unsupported working-directory clearing explicitly instead of sending an invalid patch.
- Hoist editor drafts above transient detail loading, preserve unsaved values across reconnects, and compare editable configuration rather than runtime timestamps before declaring conflicts.
- Retain unbounded editor payloads only in the Activity-scoped ViewModel, never in Android saved-instance Binder state; rotation keeps the draft while process death and ordinary navigation clear it safely.
- Expose delete-after-run only for one-shot schedules and clear it when switching to a recurring schedule, matching the Gateway deletion contract.
- Block stale saves when the gateway changes the same job, require an explicit Revert, and keep retry available after transient detail-load failures.

## User Impact

Android Settings now supports cron job details, run history, run now, editing, enable/disable, and deletion. Read-scoped connections can inspect jobs and history; mutation controls become available only with admin scope. Run results distinguish completed, queued, skipped, and rejected outcomes instead of reporting every response as success.

target.title: Draft: add CLI catalog views
target.body:
## Summary

This draft implements the CLI catalog direction from the RFC:

- RFC PR: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/32
- RFC file: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/codex/cli-catalog-overlay-rfc/rfcs/0016-cli-catalog-overlay.md

It adds a read-only `openclaw catalog` inventory over existing OpenClaw command/tool surfaces. The catalog is not a dispatcher, policy engine, runtime hook, or replacement registry. Existing CLI commands, routed operations, plugin commands, tools, and node/operator paths still own validation, permissions, confirmation, execution, and results.

## Source Registry Additions

The source-registry change is intentionally small. Registries contribute only the operational facts that are hard to infer consistently:

```ts
type CommandEffectProfile = {
  effectMode: "read" | "mutating" | "mixed";
  confirmationRequired?: boolean;
  risk?: "low" | "medium" | "high";
  commandHints?: readonly string[];
};

type CatalogExposure = {
  tier?: "public" | "internal";
};
```

Plugin CLI descriptors can also mark placeholders as `hidden` so private/local surfaces stay out of generated catalog views unless explicitly requested.

CLI descriptors still own command shape, route entries still own routing/policy shape, plugin descriptors still own plugin command shape, and node/operator commands come from node pairing/runtime declarations. The catalog layer does the N-to-1 normalization into ids, source labels, ownership, lens membership, docs/prompt/audit/operator views, and derived summaries.

## Catalog Surfaces

This branch adds:

- `openclaw catalog list` JSON/Markdown output
- runtime Commander-tree inventory for the current invocation
- opt-in plugin descriptor and command-registration inventory with `--plugin-descriptors`
- supplied node/operator command metadata
- prompt projection, including a scoped `node-operator` prompt view
- audit, test-matrix, and operator summary views
- schema fixtures, generated docs, and advisory report artifacts

## Complexity This Makes Inspectable

Current branch fixtures exercise the catalog across:

- 61 CLI descriptors
- 97 command routes
- 14 routed operations
- 5 explicit agent/tool surfaces
- supplied node/operator command metadata

The catalog command distinguishes static descriptor data from dynamic runtime/plugin data: `openclaw catalog list` collects the live Commander tree for the current invocation, and `openclaw catalog list --plugin-descriptors` includes plugin-provided CLI descriptor metadata when explicitly requested.

This matters for Scout-style deployments because the loaded runtime is not a fixed static list. The Scout container proof already sees 13 plugins, 11 enabled plugins, 2 plugin CLI commands, 8 plugin tools, and 23 allowed command/tool names from loaded config.

## Scout / Node-Mode Evidence

The live node-mode motivation comes from `gim-home/m` work:

- `gim-home/m#4045`: node-routed MCP commands such as `mcp.help`, `mcp.invoke`, `mcp.status`, and `mcp.cancel`
- `gim-home/m#4086`: filesystem node commands such as `filesystem.read`, `filesystem.write`, and `filesystem.patch`
- `gim-home/m#4088`: browser/file-open node commands such as `browser.open` and `file.openWithDefaultApp`

A node-operating agent needs a small prompt view of available node commands, argument hints, risk, confirmation, and approval boundaries that match the actual Desktop/Gateway implementation. The catalog provides that view without dumping the full inventory into prompts.

## Review Stack

This rollup PR contains the catalog stack folded together for directional review. The same work is split into fork-local draft PRs so reviewers can inspect it one layer at a time:

- PR1 foundation: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/11
- PR2 dynamic/operator lenses: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/12
- PR3 prompt projection: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/13
- PR4 schema fixtures: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/14
- PR5 generated docs: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/15
- PR6 hardening and consumer contract: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/16

Those fork-local PRs are review aids, not a request to merge from the fork. I can open the same stack against `openclaw/openclaw` separately if maintainers prefer.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli-catalog-overlay/list.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/prompt-projection.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/plugin-commands.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/schema-fixtures.test.ts src/plugins/captured-registration.test.ts src/plugins/loader.cli-metadata.test.ts src/cli/catalog-cli.test.ts --reporter=dot`
- `npm exec -- oxfmt --check <review-touched files>`
- `git diff --check`
- Clean Codex review pass for PR1-PR6 and RFC PR #32 after the source-registry effect/exposure update
- Earlier stack validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/cli-catalog-overlay-list.test.ts test/scripts/generate-cli-catalog-doc.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/schema-fixtures.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/prompt-projection.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/list.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/operator-summary.test.ts src/cli/catalog-cli.test.ts --reporter=dot`

## Notes

This is a draft for maintainer feedback on the source-registry contract, catalog command shape, dynamic/plugin/node inventory boundaries, and whether to merge as one PR or as the smaller stacked PRs.

target.title: fix: preserve prompt cache continuity in embedded sessions
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache continuity in three connected ways:

- ambient `room_event` turns changed cache-visible delivery instructions and owner-only tool schemas;
- preflight, manual, and queued compaction rebuilt prompt/tool state from the current turn's delivery mode instead of the session-stable prompt mode;
- the built-in authenticated session stream was mistaken for a custom stream, so `openai-chatgpt-responses` runs used the managed full-context SSE adapter instead of OpenClaw's native cached WebSocket continuation path.

## Fix

- Separate effective source delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode. Room events still require `message_tool_only` delivery without rewriting the cached prompt contract. Executable message tools retain the real turn mode, while Pi and Codex use the stable mode only for model-visible prompt/tool shape.
- Keep the safe room-event owner-only core-tool inventory stable across sender changes while preserving execution authorization.
- Carry the prompt-facing mode through primary runs, queued followups, Codex app-server prompt/tool builders, and every compaction entry point; compaction now rebuilds tools and system text from that stable mode. Codex keeps reusable thread instructions stable and adds strict room-event delivery guidance only to the current turn.
- Mark OpenClaw's built-in session auth wrapper and allow only that known wrapper to select the native `openai-chatgpt-responses` stream. Unmarked custom/provider streams retain their existing routing.

The native routing check is API-based, so it covers GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 without model-version branches.

## Evidence

Redacted same-session traces from the reported Discord room-event flow showed tool inventory flipping between 44 and 47 tools and cache reads collapsing to roughly 2k-10k or ceilinging around 37k-40k. With the room-event prompt/tool fix installed, warm turns with stable inventory reached roughly 49k-52k cached tokens on approximately 51k-55k context.

The route regression test reproduces the built-in auth-wrapper misclassification. A two-turn GPT-5.6 Sol WebSocket test then proves that the native provider sends the second turn with `previous_response_id` and only the new input, rather than replaying the full context.

## Validation

Validated at head `f0d85b0829d54ec9f3bda3406168f8bf2d8c0d6d` on upstream `main` `8dedb0ebcaef2bbe6dcd7b9ad137554b62ac1d21`:

- focused regression suite: 25 project test files, 1,211 tests passed, including a real targetless room-event send through the internal source-reply sink;
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, and the 120-plugin extension package boundary compile passed;
- changed TypeScript passed `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`; all generated prompt snapshots are current;
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

## Boundaries

- Effective room-event delivery remains strict; this does not make private final text visible.
- Non-owner execution of owner-only tools remains blocked.
- Custom provider/session streams are not rerouted.
- Native `auto` transport may still fall back to SSE after a real WebSocket failure; this change makes the native continuation path reachable and tested, but does not claim every upstream request will be cached.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter. Private user, channel, host, credential, and full trace identifiers were removed from the evidence.

target.title: fix(browser): filter non-page CDP targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chromium's raw `/json/list` target discovery includes workers, service workers, iframes, background pages, and real page tabs. OpenClaw filtered browser-internal URLs but could still expose a non-page target when it had a public URL, making that target selectable by browser list, focus, close, and agent flows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared CDP target filter now accepts only records whose required `type` is exactly `page`, then applies the existing browser-internal URL exclusions. The filter stays at `createProfileTabOps`, the common owner for raw CDP and Playwright-backed tab listings; the redundant URL-only filter inside the Playwright enumerator is removed.

Chromium's `/json/list` serializer always writes `type`, and the Chrome DevTools Protocol defines `TargetInfo.type` as required. Missing or malformed types therefore fail closed instead of retaining a compatibility path that would preserve this bug for non-contract providers.

## User Impact

Browser tab lists and subsequent tab actions contain real page targets only. Service workers, workers, iframes, background pages, and browser-internal pages no longer become user-facing tabs.

When \`allowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot"\` (for example, a command that uses shell redirection), \`allow-always\` is correctly excluded from the allowed decisions. The approval prompt still showed the same explanation used for an \`ask=always\` policy:

> "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable."

That is misleading because the command can be approved; it just cannot be saved as a reusable approval pattern.

Closes #97069

## What Changed

1. **`exec-approval-reply.ts`** — added optional `nonPersistableCommand` field to `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`. When true, `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` emits a distinct message explaining the command cannot be saved as a reusable pattern.

2. **`bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`** — same branch added to `buildApprovalPendingMessage` (foreground/CLI approval message path).

3. **`bash-tools.exec-types.ts`** — added `nonPersistableCommand?: boolean` to the `approval-pending` variant of `ExecToolDetails`, so the flag survives the gateway→tool-result→embedded-handler hop.

4. **`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`** — `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` accepts and passes `nonPersistableCommand` through to both the message builder and the details output.

5. **`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`** — derives and passes `nonPersistableCommand: effectiveAllowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot" && hostAsk !== "always"` to the tool-result builder.

6. **`bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`** — same derivation using `allowAlwaysPersistence` and `approvalDecisionAsk`.

7. **`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`** — `readExecApprovalPendingDetails` return type extended with `nonPersistableCommand?: boolean`; value read from details and forwarded to `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`.

8. **`exec-approval-forwarding.ts` (Telegram)** — derives `nonPersistableCommand` from `allowedDecisions` and `request.request.ask` and passes it through.

target.title: fix: allow bailian provider in resolveThinkingProfile
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The configured-model reasoning inference checks hardcode `provider === "vllm"`, excluding `bailian` (Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan) even when `compat.thinkingFormat` is correctly configured. This prevents Bailian-hosted Qwen/GLM models from being recognized as reasoning-capable, breaking `/thinking` commands and reasoning token tracking.

## Root Cause

Two locations check for `vllm` provider without considering that other providers (like `bailian`) may also serve Qwen-format models:
1. `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` — `isVllmQwenThinkingCompat()`
2. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.ts` — `readCompatThinkingFormat()`

## Fix

Extend each check to accept both `vllm` and `bailian` providers.

**Note:** The original PR also modified `extensions/vllm/thinking-policy.ts`, but this was reverted because production resolves thinking policy by provider ownership/manifest — the vLLM manifest owns only `vllm`, so `bailian` never loads this path. The change was dead code in production.

## Verified Configurations

Tested with Bailian provider using both thinking formats:

| Model | thinkingFormat | Status |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| qwen3.7-plus | openai | ✅ working |
| qwen3.6-plus | qwen | ✅ working |
| qwen3-max-2026-01-23 | openai | ✅ working |
| glm-5 | openai | ✅ working |

## Evidence

### Gateway logs showing thinking recognized:
```
agent model: bailian/qwen3.6-plus (thinking=medium, fast=off)
agent model: bailian/qwen3.7-plus (thinking=medium, fast=off)
```

### Session transcript showing thinking payloads received:
```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "thinking",
      "thinking": "The user wants me to run a cleanup script...",
      "thinkingSignature": "reasoning_content"
    },
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "🎩 **Session cleanup complete**..."
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "input": 4258,
    "output": 2240,
    "reasoningTokens": 1662,
    "totalTokens": 42594
  }
}
```

### Provider config (redacted):
```json
{
  "baseUrl": "https://coding-intl.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "qwen3.7-plus",
      "reasoning": true,
      "compat": {
        "thinkingFormat": "openai",
        "supportsUsageInStreaming": true
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "qwen3.6-plus",
      "reasoning": true,
      "compat": {
        "thinkingFormat": "qwen",
        "supportsUsageInStreaming": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Scope

This PR fixes the **custom provider** bailian path. The broader Coding Plan bundled catalog work (where models are marked non-reasoning in the bundled catalog) remains tracked in #26037.

Closes #26037

target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, `MentionShouldSkip`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions, while reusing the existing canonical `GroupRequireMention` field.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.

target.title: [Bug]: room_event forces message_tool_only despite visibleReplies=automatic, destabilizing prompt cache
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With groupChat.visibleReplies="automatic" and groupChat.unmentionedInbound="room_event", unmentioned group/channel messages are classified as room events and then forced to message_tool_only. That changes the generated system prompt inside the same session and reduces provider prompt-cache reuse.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (e085fa1) with this redacted config shape:

```json
{
  "messages": {
    "groupChat": {
      "visibleReplies": "automatic",
      "unmentionedInbound": "room_event"
    }
  }
}
```

2. In a Discord group/channel session, trigger an initial mention/session-start turn.
3. Send unmentioned group/channel messages in the same session so they arrive as room_event turns.
4. Compare generated request traces and provider prompt-cache metrics.

### Expected behavior

If visibleReplies is explicitly set to "automatic", group/channel room-event turns should preserve automatic visible final-reply semantics, or the room-event delivery mode should be separately configurable/documented. The generated system prompt should not switch between automatic final-text/NO_REPLY semantics and message_tool_only/private-final semantics inside the same session unless that switch is explicitly configured.

### Actual behavior

Observed request traces from the same session/model/cache key showed the prompt contract flipping. The session-start turn used the automatic reply prompt with `## Silent Replies`; later unmentioned room_event turns used the message-tool-only/private-final prompt. Provider cache reuse was inconsistent even with the same provider cache key.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (e085fa1)

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

### Install method

OpenClaw CLI/gateway via LaunchAgent, using ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

### Model

synthetic:hf:zai-org/GLM-5.2

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> OpenAI-compatible proxy -> Synthetic/GLM-5.2

### Additional provider/model setup details

This report is about OpenClaw prompt generation/delivery-mode selection, not provider auth. User IDs, channel IDs, hostnames, API keys, and full trace IDs are intentionally redacted. The relevant config shape is only `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies="automatic"` plus `messages.groupChat.unmentionedInbound="room_event"`.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized trace sequence from one same-session run:

| turn | kind | system prompt | prompt tokens | cached tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | session start | automatic replies + `## Silent Replies` | 46,540 | 0 |
| 2 | room_event | message-tool-only + private final text | 46,826 | 9,856 |
| 3 | room_event | message-tool-only | 47,590 | 2,048 |
| 4 | room_event | message-tool-only | 48,660 | 47,616 |

The first request and later requests used the same model and same provider cache key, but the generated system prompt changed:

- automatic prompt: 106,647 chars, sha prefix `151fdb3fb5b43caa`
- room-event prompt: 105,986 chars, sha prefix `62b9313a931f656b`

First generated prompt diff was in `## Assistant Output Directives`:


- Attach media in the final visible reply with `MEDIA:<path-or-url>`...
+ Visible source-channel output is delivered through `message(action=send)`.


Later sections also flip:


- Reply in current session -> automatically routes to the source channel ...
+ Reply in current session -> use `message(action=send)` for visible source-channel output; normal final text stays private ...


`## Silent Replies` is present in the automatic prompt and absent in the message-tool-only prompt.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Raw traces and screenshots are not attached because they contain private user/channel/account metadata. The table above is the sanitized evidence extracted from those traces.

### Impact and severity

Affected: group/channel deployments using `visibleReplies: "automatic"` with `unmentionedInbound: "room_event"`.
Severity: performance/cost regression and confusing reply-delivery semantics.
Frequency: observed on each unmentioned room_event turn in the tested session.
Consequence: lower prompt-cache reuse, higher latency/cost, and generated instructions that conflict with the configured visible-reply expectation.

### Additional information

Likely source path at e085fa1:

- `src/channels/inbound-event/classification.ts`: `unmentionedInbound: "room_event"` classifies unmentioned group/channel events as `room_event`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`: non-internal `room_event` forces `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"`.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts`: same policy path.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts` and `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`: `message_tool_only` switches the generated prompt to private-final/message-tool semantics and suppresses silent-token guidance.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.ts`: room-event prompt includes `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only`.

Possible fixes:

1. Have `room_event` respect `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "automatic"` when explicitly configured.
2. Add a separate knob, e.g. `messages.groupChat.roomEventVisibleReplies: "automatic" | "message_tool"`.
3. Document that `unmentionedInbound: "room_event"` always implies `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"`, regardless of `visibleReplies`, and warn that this changes prompt contracts/cache behavior.

My preference is option 2: ambient room-event classification and visible reply delivery should not be implicitly coupled.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were redacted before submission.

target.title: fix(slack): remember event-carried channel types so mpDMs key one session (#102676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Slack multi-party DM (`mpim`) room produces **two parallel sessions per agent**. Human-authored messages carry `channel_type: "mpim"` on the event and key `slack:group:<channelId>`; bot-authored inbound shapes omit `channel_type`, and when the `conversations.info` fill cannot resolve the type either (e.g. missing `mpim:read` scope — the fill's `catch` returns `{}`), C-prefix inference falls back to `"channel"` and keys a second `slack:channel:<channelId>` session for the same room. Modern mpDM ids are C-prefixed, so prefix inference cannot disambiguate. (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/channel-type.ts`, `message-handler/prepare.ts`; fixes #102676.)

## Why This Change Was Made

The room's type is **already known** from events previously seen for it — the fix carries that prepared fact forward instead of rediscovering (or guessing). A bounded process-local map alongside the existing channel/user caches remembers explicit `channel_type` values seen on events; the resolution chain becomes `event type → channel-info fill → remembered event type → prefix inference`. The system-event session-key resolver consults the same memory, so system events key identically (sibling surface covered).

Relative to the closed attempts on this issue: **no new network lookups** (#102752 added one and was closed for it), and it fixes the reported **C-prefixed** path mechanism itself rather than special-casing an ID prefix (#102702 only changed G-prefixed IDs). The remembered value is a *last* fallback — an explicit event type or successful `conversations.info` result always wins.

## User Impact

One session per agent per mpDM room: agents keep a single conversation context and history instead of silently splitting across `slack:group:` and `slack:channel:` keys when bots talk to each other. No config change; no new public options; no behavior change for channels whose events or info lookups already resolve a type.

## Evidence

Executed before/after (full output in the PR comment below). The regression test drives the real `prepareSlackMessage` twice on **one** monitor context (real `createSlackMonitorContext`), with `resolveChannelName` returning `{}` — a human `mpim` message for `C0MPDM42`, then a same-room message **without** `channel_type`:

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
- `CI=true pnpm oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/send.ts extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts extensions/slack/src/blocks.test-helpers.ts`
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts` (15 tests)
- `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `git diff --check`

## Verification
- Thread-scoped progress chrome converts to `reactions.add` instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

target.title: fix: keep heredoc bodies out of shell stage splits
target.body:
Closes #102875

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators reading channel tool-status footers could see heredoc body text rendered as phantom shell commands when an exec command writes multiline content with `<<EOF` and then runs a later command that fails.

In the reported Telegram footer, email body lines such as `sc-carwhi(100)` and `Gracias.` were shown as command stages, which made a normal self-correcting turn look like the agent had hallucinated broken commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

The top-level shell scanner already respected quotes and escapes, but it still visited separator characters inside heredoc bodies. This change teaches the scanner to recognize `<<` / `<<-` heredoc markers, parse quoted or escaped terminators, and skip the body until the matching terminator line before continuing normal stage and pipe splitting.

This keeps the change bounded to display-summary parsing; it does not try to validate full shell syntax or change command execution.

## User Impact

Users and operators now get clearer exec status footers for scripts that write multiline files or inline content before running follow-up commands. Heredoc body text is no longer mislabeled as failed commands, while real commands after the heredoc terminator are still summarized.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-display.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — passed, 47 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/tool-display-exec-shell.ts src/agents/tool-display.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/tool-display-exec-shell.ts src/agents/tool-display.test.ts` — passed, 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
